name: Sell-side Mandate Readiness
description: For investment banks. Scores founder-owned companies by their likelihood of needing a sell-side M&A advisor. High founder-dependence is a positive signal: it means no succession plan exists and the owner needs outside help to exit.

modules.name: Owner exit horizon proxy
modules.description: Estimates how close the founder is to a natural exit consideration window based on business age.

criteria.label: Founding year range
criteria.help_text: Source from database records or company website.

options.label: Before 1980 (business 45+ yrs old)
options.note: Founder likely 72+. High probability but watch for estate complexity or informal succession already in place.

options.label: 1980 to 1988 (business 37-45 yrs old)
options.note: Founder likely mid-to-late 60s. Strongest scoring band.

options.label: 1989 to 1997 (business 28-36 yrs old)
options.note: Founder likely 58-65. Prime window: old enough to consider exit, young enough to execute cleanly.

options.label: 1998 to 2005 (business 20-27 yrs old)
options.note: Founder likely 48-58. Possible, especially the 2001-2005 cohort. Strong signals elsewhere required for Tier 1.

options.label: 2006 to 2012 (business 13-19 yrs old)
options.note: Founder likely 43-50. Too early in most cases. Re-score in 3-5 years.

options.label: 2013 or later (under 12 yrs old)
options.note: Long-term watch list only.

modules.name: Business size and mandate viability
modules.description: Assesses whether the business is large enough to generate a viable sell-side advisory mandate.

criteria.label: Revenue estimate
criteria.help_text: Modelled estimate for private companies. Treat as order-of-magnitude only.

criteria.label: Employee count estimate
criteria.help_text: Source from database. Cross-check with LinkedIn where possible.

modules.name: Owner-operator profile
modules.description: Assesses how personally dependent the business is on the founder. For IB: high founder-dependence is a positive signal because it means no internal succession option exists.

criteria.label: Visible management layer
criteria.help_text: Check LinkedIn company page and website team or about section.

options.label: None: founder appears to be the only key person
Some: 1-2 managers present but founder still dominates
Clear: GM, COO, or VP-level management visible

criteria.label: Revenue per employee
criteria.help_text: Auto-calculated. High values indicate the founder is personally driving revenue, not a management team.

modules.name: Business profile and market position
modules.description: Assesses the quality and buyer attractiveness of the business.

criteria.label: Primary customer segment
criteria.help_text: Select the segment accounting for more than 50% of revenue.

criteria.label: Business footprint
criteria.help_text: Check the company website for number of locations.

modules.name: Behavioral harvest signals
modules.description: Observable signals indicating whether the owner is in build mode or harvest mode.

criteria.label: Active job postings
criteria.help_text: Check Indeed, LinkedIn, and the company careers page.

criteria.label: Website investment and recency
criteria.help_text: Check copyright year and whether content has been updated recently.

criteria.label: Social media activity
criteria.help_text: Check the most active platform for the business type.

bonus_rules.label: Prime founding window plus no active hiring
bonus_rules.description: Business is in the prime exit horizon and showing no capacity investment.

bonus_rules.label: Quality mandate convergence
bonus_rules.description: Right size, right market, and right age window for an attractive advisory mandate.

bonus_rules.label: Member of a relevant industry association
Owner personally visible in a local business network
No visible third-party capital or institutional backing

disqualifiers.label: Known second-generation owner already running the business
Revenue confirmed below minimum mandate threshold
Active LOI or confirmed process with another advisor
Headcount grew 30% or more in the last 18 months
Company founded post-2015 with no anomalous exit signals

name: Acquisition Target Readiness
description: For private equity firms. Scores founder-owned companies by their attractiveness as direct acquisition targets. Unlike the IB template, some management depth is a positive signal here: the business needs to be able to operate after the founder exits.

modules.name: Owner exit horizon proxy
modules.description: Estimates how close the founder is to a natural exit consideration window based on business age.

criteria.label: Founding year range
criteria.help_text: Source from database records or company website.

options.label: Before 1980 (business 45+ yrs old)
options.note: Founder likely 72+. High receptivity to a PE approach but verify successor risk and estate position.

options.label: 1980 to 1988 (business 37-45 yrs old)
options.note: Founder likely mid-to-late 60s. Strongest scoring band for PE outreach.

options.label: 1989 to 1997 (business 28-36 yrs old)
options.note: Founder likely 58-65. Prime window: open to a liquidity conversation.

options.label: 1998 to 2005 (business 20-27 yrs old)
options.note: Founder likely 48-58. Possible for partial or growth capital structures.

options.label: 2006 to 2012 (business 13-19 yrs old)
options.note: Founder likely 43-50. Too early for most outright acquisitions.

options.label: 2013 or later (under 12 yrs old)
options.note: Long-term pipeline only.

modules.name: Deal size and acquisition fit
modules.description: Assesses whether the business is in the right size range for a PE acquisition mandate.

criteria.label: Revenue estimate
criteria.help_text: Modelled estimate for private companies. Treat as order-of-magnitude only.

criteria.label: Employee count estimate
criteria.help_text: Source from database. Cross-check with LinkedIn where possible.

modules.name: Operational readiness for acquisition
modules.description: Assesses whether the business can operate after the founder's departure. For PE: some management depth is a positive signal because the business must survive the transition.

criteria.label: Visible management layer
criteria.help_text: Check LinkedIn company page and website team or about section.

options.label: None: founder is the only key person (high key-person risk)
Some: 1-2 managers present, business partially institutionalised
Clear: GM, COO, or VP-level management visible

criteria.label: Revenue per employee
criteria.help_text: Auto-calculated. High values indicate operational efficiency and pricing power.

modules.name: Business quality and revenue profile
modules.description: Assesses the defensibility and revenue quality of the business from a PE buyer perspective.

criteria.label: Primary customer segment
criteria.help_text: Select the segment accounting for more than 50% of revenue.

criteria.label: Revenue type
criteria.help_text: Check the company website for service descriptions, maintenance contracts, or subscription offerings.

options.label: Majority recurring: maintenance contracts, retainers, or subscriptions
Mix of recurring and project-based revenue

modules.name: Behavioral signals
modules.description: Observable signals indicating whether the owner is receptive to an approach.

criteria.label: Active job postings
criteria.help_text: Check Indeed, LinkedIn, and the company careers page.

criteria.label: Website investment and recency
criteria.help_text: Check copyright year and whether content has been updated recently.

criteria.label: Social media activity
criteria.help_text: Check the most active platform for the business type.

bonus_rules.label: Prime founding window plus no active hiring
bonus_rules.description: Business is in the prime exit horizon and showing no capacity expansion behavior.

bonus_rules.label: Quality acquisition convergence
bonus_rules.description: Right deal size, strong customer segment, and recurring revenue profile.

bonus_rules.label: Member of a relevant industry association
No prior PE recapitalisation or institutional backing
Located in a target geography for this fund

disqualifiers.label: Known second-generation owner already running the business
Revenue confirmed below minimum acquisition threshold
Active sale process or LOI with another buyer confirmed
Headcount grew 30% or more in the last 18 months
Business already has a PE sponsor or institutional investor

name: Strategic Buyer Propensity
description: Scores a corporate or strategic acquirer on how likely they are to want to acquire a specific target. Used by investment banks building buyer lists for a sell-side process.

modules.name: Strategic rationale
modules.description: Why would this buyer want to acquire this specific target? The strongest buyer has a clear, demonstrable reason.

criteria.label: Primary acquisition rationale
criteria.help_text: Select the most compelling reason this buyer would pursue the target. This is the most important criterion in the framework.

options.label: Clear gap fill: target addresses a known product, capability, or customer gap the buyer cannot easily build organically
options.note: The strongest rationale. Look for gaps in the buyer's product range, geographic coverage, or technical capability that the target directly fills.

options.label: Geographic expansion: target gives the buyer access to a market or region it does not currently serve
options.note: Strong rationale when the buyer has publicly stated geographic growth ambitions.

options.label: Competitor consolidation: target is a direct competitor and acquisition would increase market share or remove a threat
options.note: Common in consolidating sectors. Note that this can attract regulatory scrutiny.

options.label: Adjacency play: target is in an adjacent market with cross-sell or bundling potential
options.note: Weaker rationale unless the buyer has made similar adjacency moves before.

options.label: No clear rationale: acquisition would be opportunistic or purely financial
options.note: Corporate buyers without a clear strategic rationale rarely complete transactions.

criteria.label: Sector and business overlap
criteria.help_text: How closely does the buyer's core business relate to the target's sector?

options.label: Same sector: buyer operates the same type of business as the target
Same sector, adjacent segment: same broad sector but different sub-market or customer type
Related sector: complementary business with identifiable synergy potential

modules.name: Relative scale and absorptive capacity
modules.description: Can the buyer absorb a target of this size without it being a transformative or bet-the-company transaction? Larger buyers relative to the target have more bandwidth and lower execution risk.

criteria.label: Buyer revenue relative to target revenue
criteria.help_text: Estimate the buyer's revenue and compare it to the target's. Use database records, press coverage, or website cues for private buyers.

options.label: 10x or larger: buyer is at least 10 times the size of the target
options.note: Ideal size ratio. The acquisition is a manageable bolt-on and integration risk is low relative to the buyer's total business.

options.label: 3x to 10x: buyer is 3 to 10 times the size of the target
options.note: Good ratio. Acquisition is meaningful but not transformative.

options.label: 1x to 3x: buyer is roughly 1 to 3 times the size of the target
options.note: Caution: acquisition is material relative to buyer size. Higher integration risk and financing complexity.

options.label: Similar or smaller: buyer is roughly the same size as or smaller than the target
options.note: Transformative or reverse-merger territory. Unlikely unless the buyer has a specific thesis and external financing.

criteria.label: Prior acquisition integration track record
criteria.help_text: Has the buyer successfully integrated acquisitions before? Check for post-acquisition press releases, retention of acquired management teams, and public commentary on integration outcomes.

options.label: Proven integrator: has successfully completed and integrated multiple acquisitions
Limited experience: has made 1-2 acquisitions with no clear evidence of integration problems or success
No prior acquisitions: this would be the buyer's first transaction

modules.name: Proven acquisition behaviour
modules.description: Companies that have made acquisitions recently are far more likely to make another one. The process, board approval mechanisms, and advisor relationships are already in place.

criteria.label: Acquisitions completed in the last 3 years
criteria.help_text: Search press releases, company announcements, and M&A databases. Count only completed transactions, not rumoured or failed ones.

options.label: 3 or more: serial acquirer with an active M&A programme
1 to 2: has demonstrated willingness and ability to acquire
None recently but has prior M&A history: paused but experienced
No M&A history at all: first-time acquirer

criteria.label: M&A infrastructure
criteria.help_text: Does the buyer have a dedicated corporate development function? Check LinkedIn for corp dev titles, the company website for a business development or strategy team, and press coverage for named M&A leads.

options.label: Dedicated corporate development team: full-time M&A professionals in place
options.note: The strongest infrastructure signal. A corp dev team actively sources deals and manages pipeline.

options.label: Ad hoc through executives: M&A handled by CEO or CFO without a dedicated team
options.note: Common in smaller strategics. Deals happen but less frequently and with longer timelines.

options.label: No visible M&A infrastructure: no evidence of internal deal-making capacity

modules.name: Financial momentum
modules.description: Growing companies acquire; declining companies cut. Financial health determines both appetite and ability to complete a transaction.

criteria.label: Revenue growth trajectory
criteria.help_text: Assess the buyer's revenue growth trend from public filings, press releases, or database estimates. Growing buyers have stronger acquisition appetite and easier access to financing.

options.label: High growth: revenue growing 10% or more per year
Moderate growth: revenue growing 3 to 10% per year
Flat: revenue roughly stable year on year

criteria.label: Organisational stability
criteria.help_text: Companies undergoing major restructuring or C-suite turnover have significantly reduced bandwidth and appetite for acquisitions.

options.label: Stable: no major restructuring, leadership change, or cost-cutting programme in the last 12 months
Minor changes: some management change but core business is stable
Major disruption: active restructuring, layoffs, or C-suite turnover underway

modules.name: Access and relationship
modules.description: A warm relationship reduces the time and friction of getting a conversation started. This is an outreach variable, not a propensity variable, so it carries lower weight than strategic fit.

criteria.label: Prior relationship with the advisor or the target owner
criteria.help_text: Assess the quality of existing relationships between the advisor, the target owner, and this potential buyer.

options.label: Strong: advisor has transacted with this buyer before, or buyer has a direct relationship with the target owner
Known: advisor has met this buyer but not completed a transaction with them
No prior contact: cold approach required

criteria.label: Decision maker identified and accessible
criteria.help_text: Has the relevant decision maker (CEO, corp dev lead, or division head) been identified and is there a realistic path to contact?

options.label: Identified and accessible: decision maker is known and a warm or direct introduction is possible
Identified but cold: decision maker is known but no warm introduction exists
Not identified: the right contact inside this organisation is unknown

bonus_rules.label: Clear rationale, same sector, and proven acquirer
bonus_rules.description: The three most important signals all point in the same direction.

bonus_rules.label: Right relative scale, M&A infrastructure in place, and growing
bonus_rules.description: The buyer has the size, the capability, and the financial momentum to execute.

bonus_rules.label: Buyer has publicly stated M&A intent in the target sector (earnings call, press release, investor day)
Buyer has previously approached this target or a directly comparable asset
The sector is actively consolidating with multiple recent transactions by peer buyers

disqualifiers.label: Buyer is under financial distress, in a formal restructuring process, or has suspended M&A activity
Buyer completed a major acquisition in the last 12 months and is still integrating (bandwidth constrained)
Acquisition would likely face regulatory or antitrust challenge given buyer's existing market position
Buyer has publicly stated it is not pursuing acquisitions or is exiting this sector
Buyer has previously reviewed and passed on this specific target without material change in circumstances
